paragraphs: CalAmp sells telematics devices and cloud software that organizations use to monitor, track, and protect vehicles, equipment, and cargo. The company describes covering the whole chain, from the user experience down to the platform and the edge devices themselves. Its telematics cloud is pitched at fleet operators, logistics companies, equipment manufacturers, and the systems integrators who build on top of it.

Devices on the vehicle collect location, speed, engine health, driver behavior, and outside sensor readings in real time. The cloud then turns protocols such as CAN bus, J1939, OBD-II, and Modbus into clean, structured output. Customers pull that data through APIs, a cloud connector, or event-driven alerts. A device management layer lets administrators assign roles governing who can view, change, or execute particular management functions. Software can be prototyped, tested, and deployed to devices over the air.

CalAmp says the platform is built for commercial fleets and software providers in construction, trucking, utilities, the public sector, and equipment manufacturing. The company states it has been in business for 40 years, with thousands of customers and more than 275 approved or pending patents. For data handling it cites SOC 2 Type II certification along with GDPR and SB327 compliance.
